title: Joint and randomized equivariant observations retain the half-period blindness

joint_observation.family: An arbitrary indexed family F_i:X->Y_i of C-equivariant maps with z acting trivially on every Y_i.
joint_observation.formal_reuse: equivariantMapEquivPi identifies joint maps with component maps; componentwise z-triviality is preserved by products.
joint_observation.consequence: No number of same-kernel observables restores injectivity.

randomized_observation.channel: A C-equivariant Markov kernel K:X->Prob(Y), with C acting on probability laws by pushforward.
randomized_observation.hypothesis: z acts trivially on Y and hence on Prob(Y).
randomized_observation.consequence: Private randomness and outcome mixing do not restore the lost z-bit; a z-sensitive outcome action or explicit symmetry breaking is required.

claim_ceiling: The obstruction is closed under same-kernel observation products and equivariant probability-valued channels. It says nothing about a source-owned target with nontrivial z action, explicit symmetry breaking, or the physical interpretation of an outcome law.
